ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $66.65 surge differential to the rider's original payment method (SURGE-2/§3.3) with no driver action; separately coach the app copy team: the surge notice must state the revised fare and that the rider may cancel without penalty, and must not use "cancellation fees may apply".
ruling.reasoning: The rider booked at a 1.0× multiplier (quote $71.67, surgeable subtotal $70.20) and rode at 2.0× (surge activated 14:06:00, after the 14:04:25 booking). The multiplier rose after quoting, so SURGE-1/SURGE-2 govern. The record shows a notice was sent (in_app at 14:06:25, before the 14:08:25 arrival/14:09:00 departure) and it states the new multiplier (2.0×), but SURGE-1 requires all three items — the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare, and free cancellation. It does give a revised estimate ($141.87, which even mismatches the actual $134.77), but it says "Cancellation fees may apply", which is not the required "may cancel without penalty" and is why the rider says she "did not dare cancel". Missing an item → not properly notified → SURGE-2 row 2: refund the full surge differential. Amount = (trip multiplier 2.0 − quote multiplier 1.0) × surgeable subtotal $66.65 = $66.65; booking fee $1.47 is surge-exempt and not refunded. No route deviation is in play (actual 37.96 km vs recommended 38.009 km, within RD-1 tolerance; GPS roads match the optimal route), so the differential is a clean surge figure under SURGE-3.

element_findings.element: SURGE-1: surge notice states the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare, and free cancellation
element_findings.reason: Notice (in_app, 14:06:25, before pickup) does state the new multiplier (2.0×) and a revised estimated fare ($141.87), but the free-cancellation item is absent: it says "Cancellation fees may apply", which per the policy is not a free-cancel statement and misled the rider into not cancelling. Missing any item → not notified.

element_findings.element: SURGE-3: whether the surge differential is clean or mixed with other causes
element_findings.reason: Actual 37.96 km vs recommended/estimated 38.009 km → deviation −0.049 km, inside the 1 km tolerance (RD-1) and only map noise. No route-deviation refund arises, so the whole quote-to-actual difference is attributable to surge.

element_findings.element: RD-3/RD-5: any rider-requested stop, route or accepted destination edit
element_findings.reason: Chat contains only pickup arrangement (white dress, blue Prius, 2 min away); no named stop or route, no destination edit, and edit_destination_fee is 0.00. No segment is exempt.

element_findings.element: SAFE-1: safety screen of complaint, chat and driver statement
element_findings.reason: Read in context these concern pricing only — no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation — and the dispute type is fare_dispute.

rejected_claims.id: rider: refund the full $63.10 quote-vs-actual difference
rejected_claims.reason: SURGE-3 refunds only the surge component. Actual − quote ($134.77 − $71.67) includes the surge-exempt booking fee ($1.47), so the refund is the surge differential $66.65, not $63.10.

rejected_claims.id: driver: "Pricing is the app's, not mine. I picked up on time and drove the app route."
rejected_claims.reason: Not contradicted by the record (departure 14:09:00, actual distance 37.96 km vs recommended 38.009 km, roads match the optimal route). The driver's conduct is not the cause of the refund; the defect is in the surge notice, and no driver violation is recorded here.
